text: Every single day, every single time somebody is pushing your code to production and you're releasing a feature or an enhancement, you are making the product better or you're making the product worse, but the products never remain same.
speaker: Varun Parmar
context: Lenny asks Varun about his core product philosophies and how competition impacts product strategy. Varun explains his belief that products are never static - they're always improving or declining relative to competitors. He uses a chess metaphor to describe how every product release by you or your competitors creates relative gains or losses in the market. This framework helps product teams understand the competitive impact of their work and drives clarity around prioritization decisions.
text_ko: 매일 누군가가 코드를 프로덕션(production)에 배포하고 기능(feature)이나 개선(enhancement)을 릴리스할 때마다 제품은 좋아지거나 나빠질 뿐이고, 결코 같은 상태로 남아 있지 않아요.
text_zh: 每一天、每一次有人把代码推到生产环境 (production)，每当你上线新功能 (feature) 或做出改进 (enhancement)，你不是在让产品变好，就是在让它变糟，产品不会保持不变。
text_es: Cada día, cada vez que alguien sube tu código a producción (production) y se lanza una funcionalidad (feature) o una mejora (enhancement), estás mejorando el producto o lo estás empeorando; el producto nunca permanece igual.
key_sentence: Every release makes the product better or worse, never remains the same.
original_text: Every single day, every single time somebody is pushing your code to production and you're releasing a feature or an enhancement, you are making the product better or you're making the product worse, but the products never remain same. So with every release that your competitor is making and every release that you're making, you are either making chess points, moves against them, positive points, or you're going negative.

vocabulary.definition: An enhancement refers to an improvement or upgrade that adds value or functionality to a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, enhancements are often implemented to improve user experience, increase efficiency, or address customer feedback, thereby contributing to the overall competitiveness of a product.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'enhancement' implies a positive change, it is important to ensure that the improvements align with user needs and do not introduce new issues.

text: The success of a company is a direct relation of what the competition allows you to do.
speaker: Varun Parmar
context: Lenny discusses how Miro continues to succeed despite intense competition in the collaborative whiteboarding space. Varun shares one of his core philosophies about business growth - that a company's success is fundamentally constrained or enabled by competitive dynamics. He argues that while companies must execute well internally, the competitive landscape is often the biggest variable determining whether growth accelerates or decelerates.
text_ko: 회사의 성공은 결국 경쟁이 허용해 주는 범위 안에서 좌우돼요.
text_zh: 一家公司能否成功，很大程度上取决于竞争对手给你留了多少空间。
text_es: El éxito de una empresa depende directamente de lo que la competencia le permite hacer.
key_sentence: Success is a direct relation to what the competition allows you to do.
original_text: The success of a company is a direct relation of what the competition allows you to do. Every single instance when I looked at a company accelerated their growth or there was a deceleration of growth, it was a direct relation to what the competition allowed you to do.

vocabulary.definition: The achievement of a desired aim or purpose, often measured by the attainment of goals or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, success is frequently evaluated through metrics such as profitability, market share, and customer satisfaction, indicating the effectiveness of strategies employed.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'success' generally carries a positive connotation, it can also imply a narrow focus on financial gains, potentially overlooking other important factors like employee well-being or social responsibility.

vocabulary.definition: The rivalry among businesses or individuals to attract customers and achieve market dominance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, competition drives innovation and efficiency, compelling companies to improve their products and services to maintain or grow their market position.
vocabulary.nuance: While competition can foster improvement and innovation, excessive competition may lead to unethical practices or market saturation, which can harm the industry as a whole.

text: What you want to do is that you want to be the first one to hit the brick wall.
speaker: Varun Parmar
context: Lenny asks about Varun's product philosophies and how to balance moving fast versus moving carefully. Varun explains his belief that innovative companies should prioritize speed to discover learning faster than competitors. The 'hitting the brick wall first' metaphor means being the first to encounter and learn from failures, allowing you to course-correct while competitors are still pursuing the wrong path. This philosophy emphasizes speed as crucial for innovation leadership.
text_ko: 여러분이 하려는 건, 남들보다 먼저 벽에 부딪혀 보는 거예요.
text_zh: 你要做的，就是抢先去撞南墙。
text_es: Lo que quieres es ser el primero en chocar contra un muro.
key_sentence: Be the first to hit the brick wall; speed is the single biggest determinant.
original_text: What you want to do is that you want to be the first one to hit the brick wall. If you consider yourself as an innovation-centric company and you believe that you are building experiences that fundamentally don't exist anywhere else and you're sort of paving the way for the rest of the folks to basically get inspired with how you are building these experiences, speed is the single biggest determinant.

text: My fundamental belief here, Lenny, is that every product manager actually wants to move fast.
speaker: Varun Parmar
context: Lenny asks how to help teams move faster beyond just telling them to 'move faster.' Varun explains his philosophy that product managers are naturally driven by challenge and want to move quickly - it's their inherent personality type. He argues that slowness isn't due to lack of motivation but rather systemic roadblocks that need to be identified and removed. His approach focuses on enabling PMs to raise issues quickly so leadership can unblock them.
text_ko: 제 근본적인 믿음은, 레니, 모든 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)들이 사실 속도를 내고 싶어한다는 거예요.
text_zh: Lenny，我的基本信念是所有产品经理(product manager)其实都想快点推进。
text_es: Lenny, creo firmemente que cada responsable de producto (product manager) en realidad quiere moverse rápido.
key_sentence: every product manager actually wants to move fast.
original_text: My fundamental belief here, Lenny, is that every product manager actually wants to move fast. I think the reason why in some cases we are not able to move fast is because of roadblocks that we run into and those roadblocks can manifest themselves into technical challenges, they can manifest them in cells of organizational challenges, they could be priority challenges.

vocabulary.definition: Serving as a foundation or basis; essential and primary.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'fundamental' often refers to core principles or beliefs that guide decision-making and strategy.
vocabulary.nuance: While it implies something basic, it can also suggest a deep-seated importance that should not be overlooked.

vocabulary.definition: To act quickly or make rapid progress in decision-making or execution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup environments, 'move fast' is often associated with agile methodologies and the need to adapt quickly to market changes.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase conveys urgency and a proactive approach, but it can also imply a risk of overlooking details or quality.

vocabulary.definition: A professional responsible for the development and success of a product, overseeing its lifecycle from conception to launch.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, product managers play a crucial role in bridging the gap between engineering, marketing, and customer needs, ensuring that products meet market demands.
vocabulary.nuance: The role requires a blend of technical knowledge, business acumen, and interpersonal skills, making it both challenging and rewarding.

text: We have a motto in the product org, it's very simple, single sentence, deliver customer value faster with high quality.
speaker: Varun Parmar
context: Lenny asks about how Miro operationalizes their philosophy of moving fast and removing blockers. Varun explains Miro's core product organization motto that guides all their decisions and systems. The motto has three components: delivering customer value (measured by actual usage and metrics), moving faster (tracked through cycle times), and maintaining high quality (evaluated through design reviews). This simple statement drives their performance reviews, measurements, and organizational culture.
text_ko: 우리 프로덕트 조직(product org)은 모토가 하나 있는데, 아주 간단한 한 문장으로 "높은 품질로 고객 가치(customer value)를 더 빠르게 전달하자"예요.
text_zh: 我们产品组织（product org）有个口号，很简单，就一句话：更快为客户创造价值，同时保证高质量。
text_es: En el equipo de producto tenemos un lema muy sencillo, en una sola frase: entregar valor al cliente más rápido y con alta calidad.
key_sentence: Deliver customer value faster with high quality is our guiding motto.
original_text: We have a motto in the product org, it's very simple, single sentence, deliver customer value faster with high quality. Everything that we do, and when I say everything, everything, Lenny, from performance and reward system and measurements, everything is based on this one single statement.

vocabulary.definition: To provide or bring something to a designated recipient or location, often in the context of services or products.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, delivering refers to fulfilling commitments to customers, such as providing products or services on time and to specification.
vocabulary.nuance: While it can refer to physical goods, in a broader sense, it encompasses delivering value, results, or experiences to stakeholders.

vocabulary.definition: The perceived benefit or worth that a product or service provides to a customer, often measured against its cost.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding customer value is crucial for developing products and services that meet customer needs and drive satisfaction and loyalty.
vocabulary.nuance: Customer value is subjective and can vary significantly among different customer segments, making it essential for businesses to tailor their offerings accordingly.

vocabulary.definition: A term used to describe products or services that meet or exceed established standards of excellence and reliability.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the competitive landscape of business, high quality is often a key differentiator that can influence customer choice and brand loyalty.
vocabulary.nuance: While high quality is generally viewed positively, it can also imply higher costs, so businesses must balance quality with affordability to meet market demands.

text: You have two personas that you have to think about. The fundamental thing that you have to do is drive accountability. When you put on the persona hat of a stream leader, your number one goal that you have, is drive improvement.
speaker: Varun Parmar
context: Lenny asks about Varun's philosophy for developing product leaders at Miro. Varun explains his framework where product leaders must balance two distinct roles or 'personas.' As stream leaders, they focus on continuously improving their team's performance and outcomes. As members of the product leadership team, they must hold each other accountable for company-wide decisions and performance. This dual responsibility ensures both individual team success and collective leadership effectiveness.
text_ko: 생각해야 할 페르소나(personas)가 두 가지 있어요. 핵심은 책임(accountability)을 분명히 하는 거예요. 스트림 리더(stream leader) 역할을 맡았을 때는 최우선 목표가 개선을 이끄는 거예요.
text_zh: 你要考虑两种角色（personas）。最根本的是要推动责任落实（drive accountability）。当你戴上工作流负责人(stream leader)的“角色帽”(persona hat)时，你的首要目标就是推动改进（drive improvement）。
text_es: Tienes que pensar en dos perfiles (personas). Lo fundamental es lograr que haya rendición de cuentas (accountability). Cuando asumes el rol de líder del stream (stream leader), tu objetivo número uno es impulsar la mejora (drive improvement).
key_sentence: your number one goal that you have, is drive improvement.
original_text: You have two personas that you have to think about. The fundamental thing that you have to do is drive accountability. When you put on the persona hat of a stream leader, your number one goal that you have, is drive improvement. When you go sit in the product leadership team, your number one goal is actually to drive accountability around this.

vocabulary.definition: Serving as a basis or foundation; essential to the nature of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'fundamental' often refers to core principles or values that guide decision-making and strategy.
vocabulary.nuance: While it indicates something essential, it can also imply that other aspects may be secondary or less important.

vocabulary.definition: The obligation of an individual or organization to report, explain, and be answerable for resulting consequences.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, accountability is crucial for ensuring that team members take responsibility for their actions and outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: It carries a connotation of trust and reliability, often implying that one is held to a standard of performance.

vocabulary.definition: To actively promote or facilitate enhancements in processes, performance, or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'drive improvement' is often associated with initiatives aimed at increasing efficiency, quality, or customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase suggests a proactive and continuous effort rather than a one-time change.

vocabulary.definition: The aspect of someone's character that is presented to or perceived by others; a social facade.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and branding, 'persona' refers to the representation of a target customer or user, helping businesses tailor their strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: It implies a crafted identity that may differ from one's true self, often used in contexts requiring role-playing or strategic positioning.
